sources_read.section: §1 gates 0-5, §2 how an agent thinks, §5 task map
§5.2 transport (cursors ~20 Hz, presence, broadcast-from-database), RULE-03 (a topic is only as private as its policy), RULE-20 (cursors are ref-driven)
the realtime.messages topic policies (ws:/user:) the live: policy mirrors
007's one-socket/private-topic wiring and setAuth discipline the presence channel mirrors
the F5 event buffer (g3's same render path is already 007)
contexts[presence] ('who is here, cursors — ref-based, no store'), canvasLeaves[peer-cursors] (active, hasPainter true)

scope: The members-only live:{sessionId} topic policy (a migration), the presence channel and hook (who is here, which page), the peer-cursors canvas leaf fed by a ref + ~20 Hz throttle, and the 'leader is drawing' indicator. Out of scope: putting cursors in React state or Redux, and client broadcasts on ws:{sessionId}; g3's broadcast-from-database path is already 007's and is not reimplemented.

acceptance_criteria.text: Presence self-cleans on disconnect: peers come only from the channel's own presence state, so an untrack removes them.
No cursor value passes through useState: the leaf paints from a ref and a paint() callback the container drives; the throttle sends only on real movement.
A teammate's highlight re-renders through the same live query: unchanged from 007 (applyRemote -> Dexie -> useLiveQuery); this task adds no second render path.
The 'leader is drawing' indicator sets on a leader cursor and clears when the stroke ends (an idle timeout).
Measured latency recorded in test.json — a two-browser live-stack pass, deferred like the other browser gates.
A member cannot insert a message on ws:{sessionId}: 0006 grants send only on live:{sessionId}, so ws:/user: stay database-sent only.

open_questions: DB-Q9 (defaulted: a separate live:{sessionId} topic) — g6 implements exactly that; ws:/user: keep their database-sent-only policies.

Q8 (unanswered: the real tablet mix) — the frame-budget part of the task Gate (five simulated peers at 20 Hz without dropped frames) needs the pilot tablet; the code is written to the documented shape and the measurement is deferred.

NEW-1: the plan names `0005_live_topic.sql`, but migration 0005 is already `0005_storage_artifacts.sql` (task 003). The next free number, `0006_live_topic.sql`, is the mechanical consequence of the repo state, not a product choice; the human's go-ahead to continue is recorded here. The intent (a members-only live topic) is unchanged.

NEW-2: spec §5.2 says cursors are 'never React state'; presence (who is here) is low-frequency and may be React state, while cursors are ref+paint only. The leader indicator (g4) is a low-frequency boolean, so state there is acceptable; this split is recorded, not assumed.
risks: A client insert on ws: would let a member forge a database-change event into teammates' Dexie (DB-Q9) — mitigated by granting client send only on live: in 0006.
100 state updates a second through React drop frames (fa §3) — mitigated by the ref+paint leaf and the ~20 Hz movement-only throttle.

The live-stack RLS proof and the two-browser latency measurement cannot run without the local Supabase stack and two browsers; both are follow-ups, and the migration's SQL mirrors the proven 0004 policy shape.
